newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Officials agree on APEC membership policy.
newsitem.headline: Officials agree on APEC membership policy.

text.p: APEC ministers will consider criteria for enlarging the 18-member Pacific Rim group during two days of meetings this week, a senior Philippine official said on Thursday.
"APEC is open to admit new members. The timing, the criteria, who -- this if for ministers to decide," Philippines undersecretary for foreign affairs Federico Macaranas told a news briefing.
Russia, India and Vietnam are among countries that have expressed interest in joining APEC, which imposed a three-year moratrium on new members in 1993.

Macaranas spoke after a two-day session of senior officials from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum that laid the groundwork for a meeting of foreign and economic ministers on Friday and Saturday and the APEC summit on Monday.
Macaranas, who chaired the gathering of senior officials, said they agreed on a "Manila action plan for APEC" which represented "a giant step forward" in six areas towards free trade among members.

These covered greater market access, enhancing market access in services, providing an open investment regime, reducing the cost of doing business, building an open and efficient infrastructure sector and strengthening economic and technical cooperation.
One of the most contentious issues was the membership question and whether to present ministers with alternatives or with a package, Macaranas said.
After hours of debate, the officials finally agreed on a package which included the criteria to apply to applicants, who should be considered and when they should be admitted.
A key element, he said, would be "shadow individual action proposals (IAPs)" from applicants in which they should show a commitment to APEC's aim of free trade among members by the year 2020.
"All current members have shown a commitment to a free and open trade regime. So any applicant should show similar commitment," he said
Macaranas refused to elaborate, saying it now was up to the ministers to settle the issue.
He said another issue which had been put late to the officials covered investment and the linking of export credit agencies. "There is going to be future discussion of this matter," he added.
He said there had been some misconceptions on APEC's progress and the rates of development of individual members.
"Rather than everyone starting from one starting point, APEC wants to see everyone at an end point," Macaranas said.
